options.C: To determine the resting baseline heart rate during a hypertensive episode
options.D: To check if the kidneys are clearing aldosterone properly through the urine

explanation: We give a little bit of synthetic ACTH as a test. If the adrenal glands wake up and pump out cortisol, they're working; if they stay flat, we know there's an issue!

question: Which sign might mean a patient's bowel was accidentally injured during laparoscopy?

options.A: Mild itching around the small skin puncture sites
options.B: Severe, worsening abdominal pain and rigidity
options.C: Low-grade shoulder pain when taking a deep breath
options.D: Temporary hoarseness of the patient's voice

explanation: Spot on! If the bowel leaks contents into the tummy, it causes an infection (peritonitis) marked by severe pain and a tight, hard (rigid) belly.

question: Why is personal protective equipment placed at the very bottom of the control hierarchy?

options.A: It relies on human behavior and fails if the equipment is damaged
options.B: It is always the most expensive option available
options.C: It completely removes the hazard from the environment
options.D: It is the only method that requires worker training

explanation: PPE is considered a last resort because a mistake by the worker or a tear in the gear still leaves them exposed to the danger. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h2)

question: What is an effective way for a nurse to start talking about loss with a patient?

options.A: Changing the subject if they start to look tearful
options.B: Asking open-ended questions about how they are coping
options.C: Reminding them of all the other blessings in their life
options.D: Telling them that time heals all wounds eventually

explanation: Wonderful nursing instinct! Open-ended questions give patients the safe space to share their feelings at their own pace.

question: An intravenous drug loves fat tissue. Why might it take longer to see its full effect?

options.A: Fat cells destroy any medication that touches them
options.B: Fat tissue has a low blood supply, so the drug arrives slowly
options.C: Fat cells actively pump the medicine back into the gut
options.D: Fat tissue blocks all plasma proteins

explanation: Unlike the brain or liver, fat tissue (adipose tissue) doesn't have as many blood vessels, so drugs accumulate there at a much slower pace.

question: What is the best advice to give a young man on how to do a testicular self-exam?

options.A: Squeeze the epididymis firmly to check for inner fluid pockets
options.B: Perform the check monthly during or after a warm shower
options.C: Check the scrotum once a year during your annual medical exam
options.D: Examine the testicles only when experiencing lower back pain

explanation: Brilliant! Warm water relaxes the skin of the scrotum, making it much easier to feel around and notice any unusual lumps.

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a physical stock audit on a hospital ward?

options.A: To test the clinical skills of newly employed nurses
options.B: To compare actual items on the shelf with recorded inventory
options.C: To clean out the dust from the medication store cupboards
options.D: To dispose of all old equipment regardless of expiry date

explanation: Stock audits involve counting what is physically present to match it with what the logbook says should be there. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: Why is Type O-negative blood considered the universal red cell donor?

options.A: The blood type is the most common found in humans
options.B: The red blood cells lack A, B, and Rh antigens
options.C: The red blood cells have no hemoglobin inside them
options.D: The plasma contains high levels of protective platelets

explanation: Because Type O-negative red blood cells carry none of the major antigens, recipient antibodies have nothing to react against. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h5)

question: A mother of four girls visits the clinic complaining of constant headaches, tiredness, and sleeplessness, but tests show she is physically fine. What should you, as the nurse, keep in mind?

options.A: Nutritional deficiencies caused exclusively by eating local foods
options.B: Psychological distress related to family pressure for a male child
options.C: An undiagnosed genetic blood disorder causing sleep disturbances
options.D: A rare neurological reaction to routine postpartum vitamins

explanation: Physical complaints with no clear medical cause often mask deep emotional stress from family pressure to have a boy.

question: How do beta-hCG hormone levels usually behave in an ectopic pregnancy compared to a healthy one?

options.A: They rise much slower or fail to double at expected rates
options.B: They disappear completely from the bloodstream within hours
options.C: They double much faster than in any normal intrauterine pregnancy
options.D: They remain perfectly steady without any changes at all

explanation: Ectopic pregnancies often produce abnormal hormone patterns, failing to double as quickly as a healthy intrauterine pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h5)

question: How does low educational background directly affect a client's use of family planning?

options.A: It prevents them from walking long distances
options.B: It makes reading instruction leaflets difficult
options.C: It automatically lowers blood pressure
options.D: It changes their blood group

explanation: Spot on! Low reading skills can make it hard for a client to understand written package instructions and warnings.

question: How can chronic stress lead to heart disease over time?

options.A: By slowing down the heart rate to dangerous levels
options.B: By causing sudden enlargement of heart valves
options.C: By maintaining high blood pressure and damaging arterial walls
options.D: By reducing the amount of blood pumped by the heart

explanation: When stress hormones keep your blood pressure high day after day, it slowly damages your blood vessels, making it easier for plaque to build up.

question: Which workplace strategy best helps nurses cope with moral distress during end-of-life care?

options.A: Ignoring difficult ethical situations to focus only on physical tasks
options.B: Avoiding all discussions with dying patients and their families
options.C: Participating in regular clinical debriefings and ethics rounds
options.D: Accepting every medical order without questioning its futility

explanation: Talking it out helps! Team debriefings and ethics meetings give nurses a safe space to share their feelings, process tough cases, and find support.

question: What is the main purpose of carrier testing in clinical practice?

options.A: To measure the exact physical strength of a newborn baby
options.B: To identify healthy individuals who carry a recessive gene mutation
options.C: To diagnose an advanced degenerative disorder in the elderly
options.D: To cure a genetic disease before it starts showing symptoms

explanation: Carrier testing is designed for people who do not have symptoms themselves but want to know if they could pass a recessive condition to their children. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h4)

question: What are the earliest vital sign clues that a patient might be bleeding internally after a biopsy?

options.A: Sudden high blood pressure and a very slow pulse
options.B: Falling blood pressure and a fast heart rate
options.C: Rising fever and flushed skin
options.D: Slow, deep breathing with high oxygen levels

explanation: Spot on! When blood is lost inside, blood volume drops. The heart beats faster to make up for it, while blood pressure starts to slide down.

question: The neural tube, which forms the brain and spinal cord, develops from which germ layer?

options.A: Endoderm
options.B: Trophoblast
options.C: Mesoderm
options.D: Ectoderm

explanation: Since the nervous system links closely with the skin and outer structures, it comes right from the ectoderm layer. Excellent recall!

question: Why might a surgeon need to perform a craniectomy (removing a piece of the skull) after severe brain trauma?

options.A: To remove the primary injury site completely
options.B: To permanently cure the patient's concussion
options.C: To relieve dangerous pressure caused by brain swelling
options.D: To clean out surface dirt from a skull fracture

explanation: You got it! Taking off a piece of the skull gives a swollen brain room to expand outward instead of crushing vital areas inside.

question: When giving ear drops to an adult patient, how should you pull the outer ear (pinna)?

options.A: Forward and down
options.B: Down and back
options.C: Straight outward
options.D: Up and back

explanation: A classic clinical tip! For adults, pulling the pinna up and back straightens out the wiggly ear canal so the drops flow smoothly all the way down.

question: What is the first physical action a nurse should take when non-reassuring foetal heart patterns appear?

options.A: Change the mother's position to her side
options.B: Prepare the operating room for a caesarean section
options.C: Administer a strong dose of pain medication
options.D: Encourage the mother to push with all her strength

explanation: Turning the mother to her side takes pressure off major blood vessels, instantly improving blood return to the heart and placental blood flow. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h5)

question: What makes William Worden's grief theory different from the usual stage models?

options.A: It applies exclusively to elderly patients
options.B: It focuses only on the physical symptoms of dying
options.C: It states that grief ends completely within six weeks
options.D: It views grief as active tasks the person must work through

explanation: Great job! Instead of just passing through passive stages, Worden's model sees grief as a series of active steps or tasks the person works through to adapt.

question: What key advice should you give a patient with mild COVID-19 who is well enough to stay home?

options.A: Visit crowded public areas to build natural community immunity
options.B: Stop wearing a mask immediately once the fever drops
options.C: Avoid drinking fluids so that coughing spells decrease
options.D: Stay home in isolation to avoid spreading the virus to others

explanation: You nailed it! Self-isolating at home is the best way to protect your family members and community from catching the virus.

question: A pregnant patient reports severe chest pain spreading down her left arm. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Report it immediately for cardiac evaluation
options.B: Suggest she take a strong antacid tablet right away
options.C: Reassure her that this is normal third-trimester heartburn
options.D: Advise her to lie down and drink cold milk

explanation: Chest pain spreading to the arm is a red flag for the heart! Never brush it off as simple heartburn.

question: A patient scheduled for a sigmoidoscopy takes Warfarin daily for their heart. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Tell the patient to double their dose.
options.B: Notify the ordering doctor right away about the blood thinner.
options.C: Tell the patient to stop all meds forever.
options.D: Do the enema prep without mentioning the medication.

explanation: Safety first! Blood thinners raise the risk of bleeding if a biopsy is taken, so the doctor needs to review this beforehand.

question: Which type of cancer risk is actually lowered by long-term use of combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: Stomach cancer
options.B: Ovarian cancer
options.C: Skin cancer
options.D: Lung cancer

explanation: By resting the ovaries and stopping ovulation over time, birth control pills actually help protect against ovarian and endometrial cancers. A nice little bonus benefit!

question: As a nurse, why should you understand lab values instead of just looking at the high or low flags?

options.A: Because laboratory printers frequently misprint the normal reference ranges
options.B: Because nurses are legally required to diagnose medical diseases
options.C: Because numbers help the nurse anticipate complications and plan safer care
options.D: Because doctors do not look at blood reports until discharge

explanation: You're not just memorizing numbers for an exam! Connecting lab values to real body signs helps you spot trouble early and keep your patient safe.

question: Which animal is the very first home (intermediate host) for the Paragonimus parasite?

options.A: Domestic pig
options.B: Aquatic bird
options.C: Freshwater crab
options.D: Freshwater snail

explanation: Great job! The parasite's early larvae need to enter a freshwater snail first to grow and develop through their early stages.

question: When you take over a new shift, what do you accept regarding your assigned patients?

options.A: Financial responsibility for their hospital bills
options.B: Legal and professional accountability for their care
options.C: The obligation to discharge them by the end of the day
options.D: Full ownership of all past medical errors made by doctors

explanation: Taking over patients means you are now officially responsible for watching over them and giving them proper care during your shift. You've got this!

question: What does 'parenteral route' mean when talking about how diseases spread?

options.A: Entry through a break in the skin via needles or sharps
options.B: Inhalation of airborne droplets through the nose
options.C: Ingestion of contaminated food or drinking water
options.D: Spread through direct skin-to-skin physical contact

explanation: Think of parenteral as bypassing the skin barrier completely—usually when a contaminated needle or sharp punctures the tissue directly. Simple and clear!

question: What is your very first nursing action when a patient has an active front-of-the-nose nosebleed?

options.A: Instruct the patient to blow the nose gently to clear out old blood clots
options.B: Tilt the patient's head backward and pack both nostrils tightly with dry cotton
options.C: Lay the patient flat on their back and apply ice packs directly over the forehead
options.D: Have the patient sit upright and lean forward while pinching the soft part of the nose

explanation: You nailed it. Leaning forward stops blood from trickling down their throat, and pinching the soft part applies direct pressure to close off the bleeding vessels.

question: When should you definitely NOT perform a rectal washout?

options.A: A stable history of controlled high blood pressure
options.B: Temporary loss of appetite for two days
options.C: Recent bowel surgery with an active anastomosis
options.D: Mild chronic constipation in an elderly adult

explanation: Never force fluid into a fresh surgical connection (anastomosis)! The pressure could cause it to break open, leading to dangerous leaks.

question: You suspect a patient is skipping their blood pressure meds because their readings are still high. How should you start this chat?

options.A: I know you forgot your pills because your blood pressure is still high.
options.B: If you do not start taking your medicine today, you will suffer a stroke.
options.C: Why are you wasting your money by refusing to take your prescribed drugs?
options.D: Many people find it hard to take pills every day; tell me about your routine.

explanation: Brilliant choice! Normalizing the struggle takes away shame and helps the patient open up honestly to you.

question: Why do we take a thorough health history before checking a patient's eyes, ears, nose, and throat (EENT)?

options.A: To find out their exact insurance coverage
options.B: To diagnose complex systemic diseases on our own
options.C: To spot key symptoms and guide the physical exam
options.D: To replace the physical exam completely

explanation: Spotting early clues like pain or discharge helps you and the doctor know exactly where to focus during the physical check. Great job!

question: Why must raw meat always go on the lowest shelf of the fridge?

options.A: So it is faster for the cooks to grab
options.B: To keep it closest to the fridge cooling fan
options.C: To stop meat juices from dripping onto other foods below
options.D: Because raw meat likes warmer spots than veggies

explanation: Gravity is sneaky! If raw meat drips onto ready-to-eat foods below it, it spreads harmful germs. Always keep raw meat at the bottom.

question: Why do patients who receive repeated blood transfusions end up with an overload of iron in their bodies?

options.A: Transfused red blood cells immediately break down in the digestive tract
options.B: The human body lacks an active physiological mechanism to excrete excess iron
options.C: Kidneys filter out red blood cells but trap all the iron in the nephrons
options.D: The liver actively manufactures iron whenever foreign blood is introduced

explanation: Our bodies are great at holding onto iron, but we have no natural way to get rid of extra amounts. Every transfusion adds more iron, which builds up over time.

question: What does the clinical term 'undetectable viral load' mean for a patient on ART?

options.A: The immune system has stopped producing white blood cells
options.B: The virus has completely disappeared from every organ in the body
options.C: The amount of HIV in the blood is too low for standard lab tests to measure
options.D: The patient no longer needs to take their daily medications

explanation: An undetectable viral load means the medication has successfully suppressed the virus so standard blood tests cannot find it. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h2)

question: A patient complains of sharp pain in their lower right tummy. Which organ should a nurse suspect right away?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Heart
options.D: Appendix

explanation: Classic clinical scenario! The appendix is typically tucked away in the lower right quarter of the abdomen.

question: Why is keeping the hospital environment safe such a big priority when caring for a GPI patient?

options.A: Patients go completely blind and cannot find their way around.
options.B: Confusion and poor body balance put them at high risk for falls.
options.C: Patients can easily spread the infection to staff through casual touch.
options.D: Bright lights can trigger sudden seizures.

explanation: That's correct! Because brain changes mess with both thinking and physical balance, our main nursing goal is keeping the patient safe from nasty falls.

question: Why is it important to ask patients if they have visited patent medicine vendors when taking their history?

options.A: Hospital records automatically track all purchases made in private shops
options.B: Many informal vendors administer unsterile injections that patients forget to mention
options.C: Patent medicine vendors are legally required to report side effects
options.D: Patients only get infections when visiting registered general hospitals

explanation: Patients often think of informal drug purchases as casual and might forget to mention them. Asking directly helps us catch hidden risks like unsterile shots!

question: What must you check before giving a patient water after an upper GI scope?

options.A: That the patient's gag reflex has fully returned
options.B: That the patient's blood pressure is above normal
options.C: That the doctor has reviewed all laboratory results
options.D: That the patient has passed normal flatus

explanation: Their throat is usually numbed during the test. Checking for the gag reflex ensures they won't choke when they finally take a sip of water!

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take before preparing medications?

options.A: Perform hand hygiene
options.B: Check the hospital bed
options.C: Pour water into a cup
options.D: Open the patient chart

explanation: Hand hygiene is the primary step in infection control to prevent spreading germs to clean medication supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h5)

question: A patient expresses intense anger toward the nursing staff and complains about everything. What is the most likely root cause of this behavior?

options.A: An allergic reaction to their routine pain medication
options.B: A deliberate attempt to shorten their hospital stay
options.C: A personal dislike for the specific nurse caring for them
options.D: A deep feeling of losing control over their life and illness

explanation: Anger in terminal illness frequently masks helplessness and frustration over losing independence and control. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h2)

question: What is a key sign that a patient's grief may be 'complicated' rather than normal?

options.A: Experiencing fatigue during the first few weeks after loss
options.B: Feeling sad and crying on the anniversary of the loss
options.C: Intense debilitating symptoms lasting beyond six months
options.D: Wanting to talk about the deceased person frequently

explanation: You're doing great! While everyone grieves at their own pace, severe symptoms that completely disrupt life after six months point toward complicated grief.

question: Why do midwives often prefer a continuous running stitch instead of separate knots for a second-degree tear?

options.A: They are associated with less short-term postpartum pain.
options.B: They prevent the wound from healing by secondary intention.
options.C: They require significantly more suture material to complete.
options.D: They eliminate the need for any local anesthesia during repair.

explanation: Studies show that continuous stitching leaves less foreign material behind in the wound, meaning the mother hurts less afterward.
